translation_en: “Ah! Forgive me! You are the only woman who attracts me. I’ve been foolish and cruel! **I love you**, I will always love you!… What’s wrong? Tell me!”
larger_context_summary: This is Léon addressing Emma during the later, increasingly strained phase of their adulterous affair. His apology indicates that something in his recent conduct has hurt or alarmed her, although the displayed passage alone does not specify the precise offense. Léon presents Emma as uniquely desirable, acknowledges his own foolishness and cruelty, and tries to reassure her of both present and lasting devotion. In the wider novel, their relationship has ceased to provide the uncomplicated romantic escape Emma imagined: secrecy, disappointment, emotional volatility, and Emma’s worsening financial crisis place mounting pressure on it.
interpretive_commentary: The declaration most clearly asserts Léon’s present emotional state, and its unqualified, direct form makes strong truth-conditional force plausible even if readers suspect exaggeration, strategy, or self-deception. Possible insincerity would concern whether the claim is true, not what kind of claim he presents it as. The surrounding apology gives the words some relationship-shaping force: he is seeking forgiveness and attempting to repair or reaffirm the affair. That force remains limited because “I love you” does not by itself establish a new bond or explicit obligation; the neighboring “I will always love you” carries more of the possible pledge. Exclamation marks, self-reproach, and the urgent question make the delivery intense, but intensity is not the same as reflexive expressive force. The avowal remains a composed proposition embedded in a persuasive reassurance rather than an involuntary emotional cry.
